correctness.rationale: The normalized worst-convex-body error is exactly half the uniform cosine-support discrepancy, by the planar Cauchy surface-area formula and limiting skinny rectangles. Every full-dimensional zonogon of a normalized positive rule has perimeter four. A contained tangential polygon obtained from its facet normals, together with Jensen convexity of tangent, gives the sharp origin-centered inradius inequality \(r\le\cot(\pi/(2N))/N\), with equality only for the regular \(2N\)-gon and uniform weights. The uniform rule's circumradius plus inradius is below \(4/\pi\), so its lower discrepancy is the actual worst error. Near optimality implies \(r\ge r_N-2\delta\); the global derivative inequality \(\tan''y\ge2y\) yields squared angular deviation at most \(24\delta/[x r_N(r_N-2\delta)]\). A four-gap symmetric tangential perturbation has \(\delta(t)=r_N^2\tan''(x)t^2/8+O(t^4)\) and angular deviation squared exactly \(4t^2\), proving optimality of the exponent. The written analytical arguments cover every integer \(N\ge2\); 2944 deterministic sample checks corroborate normalization and expansions without replacing infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The originating full text arXiv:2609.05869v1 (16 pages) proves the general defect identity, impossibility of exact Cauchy quadrature, and O(1/t) design error, but does not state an optimal normalized positive N-node planar constant, uniqueness or quantitative angular stability. Full arXiv HTML for Gui-Hu-Li arXiv:2607.28768v2 reveals a Jensen angular deficit for torsional rigidity at fixed polygon area, not the same Cauchy perimeter-sampling minimax. Inspected Akiyama-Kamae width deviation work uses L2 shape variation, not uniform over convex-body inputs. Targeted comparisons with indexed published mathematical findings did not identify an equivalent or dominating statement. Classical regular-polygon tangent geometry is an acknowledged essential ingredient; an unindexed equivalent quadrature theorem remains a residual risk. Audet–Hansen–Messine (2009) solve related maximum-width questions over unrestricted fixed-sided polygons, but their general bound differs from the sharp regular centrally symmetric even-polygon ratio and their actual full-text results contain neither the finite Cauchy node minimax problem nor its angular-error stability.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical derivation of the same sharp N-node Cauchy quadrature value or angular stability is not excluded by searches.

value.rationale: The originating paper asks for exact and approximate finite directional reconstruction of integral-geometric averages. In the first obstructed kernel, classical planar Cauchy brightness, this theorem solves the natural complete optimal positive fixed-budget rule in closed form for every integer \(N\ge2\), identifies unique nodes and weights, improves the available \(O(N^{-1})\) design-estimate to sharp \(\pi/(12N^2)\), and bounds directional instability from normalized excess error with best-possible square-root order. The value is the relevant minimax and stability law; numerical correctness or search novelty alone would not suffice.
